correctness.rationale: Over algebraically closed fields p=11,13 and smooth b(a²−4b)≠0, the three holomorphic differentials and coefficient extraction via Cartier yield p=11 off-diagonal Prym entries 3a and −a b²(a²−4b)², and p=13 diagonal entries 2b²(a²−4b)²(a²+5b) and 6(a²+5b), with elliptic quotient coefficient nonzero in p=13. For p=11 the Prym zero is a=0 (j=1), and for p=13 a²+5b=0 (j=−1). The determinant reductions 5j²(1−j), 4j²(j+1)², and the p-divisible splitting by a prime-to-p two-isogeny give the stated Newton slopes, p-ranks and a-numbers. Independently inspected polynomial_power and Cartier coefficient checker; finite Fp checks do not prove algebraically closed classification, which follows from the symbolic factorizations.

evidence: Published October 18 uniform theorem gives complete p-rank/a-number for EVERY p>=5 and all smooth t, with the exceptional roots of H_p; October 25 theorem also gives the four Newton-polygon cases and the same degree-two elliptic–Prym isogeny.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For p=11 (6m+5,m=1), the published H_11(t) is proportional to t: the unique root t=0 maps to j=1 and Cartier rank 0. For p=13 (6m+1,m=2), H_13(t) is proportional to t^2-2: two roots ±sqrt(2) map to j=-1 and rank 1 for the full Jacobian (superspecial Prym with ordinary elliptic factor). Thus exact nonordinary strata and full Newton polygons follow as special cases.

evidence: For p=11 the Prym matrix swaps two entries each divisible by t, and j=1-t²: a double t zero becomes a simple j zero. For p=13 each of two diagonal Prym entries is proportional to H_13(t); the determinant contains H_13(t)^2 and j+1=2-t²: it has a double j zero. The published Cartier coefficients and isogeny determine these multiplicities.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The remaining normalized determinant leading constants are basis/coordinate substitutions in the published explicit Cartier formula and can be directly checked against the source. No new independent theorem remains merely by recording p=11,13 or a simple/double zero in the j coordinate.
